answer: Use a karst-style payout graph: each buyer-funded escrow has one outlet, a receipt redeemable for nectar by one worker only. A proposed contract marks receipts spent on delivery and pays only from that escrow, not per key. A farm can forge fake jobs with its own deposits, its cheapest counter, but each extra paid identity needs a distinct buyer-sized escrow and a nonrefundable marketplace fee. If the farm self-funds, the payout returns its own principal minus the fee; if it replays a receipt, the contract forfeits that payout. Without new outside buyers, clones just split a fixed pool.
